site_name: Apple Mesa global data command center (former GT Advanced plant), 3740 S Signal Butte Rd, Mesa, AZ 85212
year_evidence_quote: Apple took operational control of the building in October 2015 and converted it to a data center that began servicing customers in March 2017.
year_site_match: Apple's own report, section headed 'Mesa, Arizona', describes 'our global command center in Mesa, Arizona' and a building Apple took control of in October 2015 and converted to a data center. Data Center Knowledge and MacRumors (both Feb 2, 2015) identify that building as the former GT Advanced 1.3 million sq ft plant in Mesa. No page I opened gives the Signal Butte Rd street address; the tie rests on Apple having one Mesa data center.
verification: The claimed 2018 is NOT supported as a start year. The FOX 10 article (Aug 15, 2018) says only that Apple services 'are now running through this building in Mesa' and gives no start date. Apple's 2017 Environmental Responsibility Report (PDF dated Apr 18, 2017, covering FY2016) shows the site operating earlier. The report is internally inconsistent by one year: the body text says the Mesa center 'came online in 2016', while the chart heading says '100% renewable since opening March 2017' and the footnote says it 'began servicing customers in March 2017'. I report 2017 because it is the month-specific statement and matches the 'serving traffic' test; 2016 is the alternative if 'came online' is the preferred test. Confidence is set to medium, not high, because of that conflict. The 2018 and 2019 Apple reports exceeded the fetch size limit and were not read.
